articles.summary: The department expects the projects will add 23 GW in grid capacity and will come online in “record time” to improve the existing transmission system.

articles.title: On clean energy, bigger is not always better
articles.summary: When Congress revisits clean-energy tax policy, lawmakers should restore incentives for locally driven solar and storage projects, writes Edward Yim at Lawyers for Good Government.

articles.title: New York audits utility AI use, cites risk in ‘growing dependency’
articles.summary: Increasing use of AI systems to manage public utilities creates new risks for critical infrastructure, regulators said.

articles.title: Microgrids must push beyond pilots, into everyday grid operations: panel
articles.summary: EPRI’s Jackie Baum says microgrids have to do more than sit idle for emergencies. “The majority of the time, the power is on,” she said, urging utilities to use those resources.

articles.title: FERC has options for modernizing PJM’s governance
articles.summary: The commission’s jurisdiction over transmission governance allows it to modify filing-rights allocations and adjust the PJM Interconnection’s nominating committee, writes Harvard Law’s Ari Peskoe.

articles.title: FERC rejects ComEd’s cancellation of PowerHouse Hillwood data center contract
articles.summary: A 1.8-GW, $20 billion data center planned by PowerHouse Hillwood was underpinned by a $1 letter of credit — “less than the price of a cup of coffee” — that drew skepticism from FERC Commissioner David LaCerte.

articles.title: Efforts to curb data center speculation gain ground across the US
articles.summary: Large-load tariffs and other measures to weed out speculative projects are taking shape. Public backlash to data centers, shifting state-level policies and the utility profit model are complicating those efforts, stakeholders say.

articles.title: Lower energy costs, community benefits drive 30% battery growth rate: RMI
articles.summary: The report arrives as the energy storage industry faces headwinds from tariffs, Treasury regulations and new White House restrictions on foreign-made bulk electrical components.

articles.title: It’s time for utility bill reform
articles.summary: Programs that serve broad public purposes should be financed through state general funds rather than hidden in your electric bill, writes Marc Brown at the Consumer Energy Alliance.

articles.title: Tips from China's 56-month nuclear construction schedule
articles.summary: The President of China's State Nuclear Power Technology Corporation, Ma Yuanhua, shared their "thinking and practice" in developing a fleet-based construction process which now has a target of 56 months for new nuclear power units.

articles.title: Deep Fission completes borehole demonstration
articles.summary: A full-sized prototype of the canister that will hold the Gravity reactor has been installed and then retrieved from a borehole using standard equipment already in commercial service in the drilling industry.

articles.title: Groundwork begins for demonstration Hualong One 2.0 units
articles.summary: Site levelling and excavation work for the second phase of the Jinqimen nuclear power plant in China's Zhejiang Province has begun, China National Nuclear Corporation announced. The site will eventually house six HPR1000 (Hualong One) units.

articles.title: Indiana to get its first power-producing nuclear reactor
articles.summary: A commercially owned and operated micromodular reactor is to be installed at Naval Weapons Station Crane, becoming the US Navy's first shore-based advanced micromodular reactor as well as the state of Indiana's first power-producing reactor.

articles.title: eVinci sets temperature record during zero-power criticality tests
articles.summary: Westinghouse says the completion of zero-power high-temperature criticality testing for the microreactor, which saw it reach criticality at 663 degrees Celsius, is a defining milestone in the programme's build-test-learn development journey.

articles.title: China launches Global Network for SMR Innovation
articles.summary: China Atomic Energy Authority has launched the Global Network for SMR Innovation with the aim of supporting small modular reactor technology progress, standards and deployment "helping make nuclear energy safer, more affordable and more accessible in support of climate action and sustainable development".

articles.title: First SMR funding agreed by European Investment Bank
articles.summary: The European Investment Bank is to invest up to EUR40 million (USD46 million) in Finland's small modular reactor company Steady Energy, whose LDR-50 reactor is designed specifically for district heating networks.

articles.title: US funding for Thai SMR feasibility study
articles.summary: The Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand has signed an agreement with the US Trade and Development Agency for a feasibility study on the deployment of US small modular reactor technologies in Thailand.

articles.title: Blue Energy submits first construction application to NRC
articles.summary: Blue Energy has submitted the first part of its construction permit application to the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission for its planned gas-to-nuclear project in Texas.

articles.title: Smolensk's planned new units get environmental approval
articles.summary: The licence justification materials for two new units at the next phase of Smolensk Nuclear Power Plant in Russia have had a positive verdict from Russia's State Environmental Expertise.

articles.title: Third unit at Changjiang site commissioned
articles.summary: Unit 3 of the Changjiang nuclear power plant in China's island province of Hainan has entered commercial operation. The unit is the first of two Hualong One (HPR1000) reactors being constructed as Phase II of the plant.

articles.title: Natural draft cooling tower is preferred JEK2 option
articles.summary: A feasibility study of four cooling tower options for Slovenia's proposed JEK2 new nuclear project has proposed a natural draft cooling tower of between 193 metres and 198 metres.

articles.title: Containment tests completed at Lufeng unit 5
articles.summary: Tests to check the integrity of the containment structure have been completed at unit 5 of the Lufeng nuclear power plant in China's Guangdong province. The unit is the first of two Hualong One (HPR1000) reactors under construction at the site.

articles.title: Akkuyu 1 set for next stage of pre-commissioning activities
articles.summary: The first unit at Turkey's Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant is being prepared for the reactor's next stage of pre-start-up testing.

articles.title: Nuward targets 10 SMRs in five EU countries
articles.summary: As the European Industrial Alliance on SMRs says it is now assessing a second round of applications, Nuward's CEO has said that it aims to start construction of the first of an initial fleet of 10 units in 2030.

articles.title: Indian plants celebrate fuel loading milestones
articles.summary: As fuel loading begins at Rajasthan Atomic Power Project unit 8, Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd has started geotechnical investigations for the next two units at the plant. Meanwhile, fuel loading has begun at Kaiga unit 1 as the unit begins the process to return to service after refurbishment.

articles.title: Power start-up for Mochovce 4
articles.summary: Slovakia's Mochovce 4 began power generation at 15:33 on Monday, which operator Slovenske elektrárne describes as the last major stage before the unit is put into operation.

articles.title: GE Vernova, Hitachi, SGE and Samsung C&T sign BWRX-300s MoU
articles.summary: An agreement to work together to identify and develop market opportunities for the deployment of BWRX-300 small modular reactors in Europe was signed on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

articles.title: Škoda JS to supply control rod drives for Rolls-Royce SMR's reactors
articles.summary: Czech company Škoda JS has been chosen as sole supplier of control rod drive mechanisms for Rolls-Royce SMR's future small modular reactors.

articles.title: SGE confident of UK SMR fleet prospects
articles.summary: The team behind plans for a fleet of 14 BWRX-300 small modular reactors in the UK says they are confident of the economic model and supply chain capability to deliver these units.
